preamble: Each domain question draws from the complete medical record. Points reflect diagnostic weight. Cost reflects typical test burden: Small = existing record / standard echo  |  Medium = targeted test or genetic panel ($200–$1,500)  |  Large = advanced imaging CT/MRI/RHC ($1,500–$5,000+)

questions.question: Is there LV dilation (LVEDd Z-score >2 in children; >5.5 cm in adults) with global systolic dysfunction on 2D echo?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — LV dilation + reduced EF is the primary diagnostic criterion for DCM; Z-score >2 corrects for body surface area in pediatric patients

questions.question: Is LV ejection fraction (LVEF) <45% (or <50% by biplane Simpson in symptomatic patients) on echo or cardiac MRI?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — LVEF <45% with dilation defines DCM in the absence of another cause; distinguishes from HFpEF; <35% triggers ICD consideration

questions.question: Is there functional mitral regurgitation (FMR) from annular dilation and papillary muscle displacement?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — FMR is present in ~50% of DCM and contributes to hemodynamic deterioration; severity worsens with progressive LV dilation

questions.question: Does CMR confirm LV dilation, EF, and distinguish DCM from ischemic cardiomyopathy (subendocardial vs. mid-wall fibrosis pattern)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — CMR is gold standard for DCM phenotyping; ischemic LGE (subendocardial/transmural) vs. DCM pattern (mid-wall septal stripe or diffuse) guides etiology and prognosis

questions.question: Is there mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on CMR indicating myocardial fibrosis (present in ~30% of DCM)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — mid-wall septal LGE in DCM is an independent predictor of SCD, arrhythmia, and adverse outcome; presence supports prophylactic ICD implantation

questions.question: Has genetic testing identified a pathogenic variant in TTN (most common: ~20–25% of familial DCM), LMNA, SCN5A, MYH7, MYBPC3, RBM20, FLNC, or PLN?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — TTN truncating variants are most common; LMNA mutations carry highest arrhythmia/SCD risk requiring early ICD; confirms genetic DCM and enables cascade family screening

questions.question: Is there a first-degree relative with confirmed DCM (familial DCM present in 20–50% of cases when systematic family screening performed)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — family history changes classification to familial DCM; triggers echo screening of all first-degree relatives; increases likelihood of identifying a causative gene

questions.question: Is there an associated genetic syndrome or systemic condition (Duchenne/Becker MD, Barth syndrome, Emery-Dreifuss MD, Friedrich's ataxia, hemochromatosis)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — syndromic DCM carries distinct prognosis and management (e.g., Barth: 3-methylglutaconic aciduria, neutropenia; Duchenne: corticosteroid benefit, respiratory monitoring)

questions.question: Is there LBBB (QRS ≥120 ms with left bundle morphology) or non-specific intraventricular conduction delay (IVCD) on ECG?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — LBBB in DCM predicts poor mechanical coordination and LV dyssynchrony; QRS ≥150 ms with LBBB is the strongest predictor of CRT response

questions.question: Is there PR prolongation (first-degree AV block) or advanced AV block, particularly in LMNA-positive DCM?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — LMNA cardiomyopathy has a classic phenotype: AV block + DCM + arrhythmia; PR prolongation is often the earliest LMNA manifestation and prompts prophylactic ICD

questions.question: Is there non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (NSVT) on Holter or prolonged event monitor?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — NSVT in DCM with LVEF <35% is a major ICD indication; LMNA-positive patients with NSVT have especially high SCD risk even at higher EF

questions.question: Is NT-proBNP >1000 pg/mL (or BNP >200 pg/mL) significantly elevated reflecting LV wall stress?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — NT-proBNP elevation in DCM correlates with NYHA class, LVEF, and prognosis; serial monitoring guides therapy titration and guides heart failure hospitalization risk

questions.question: Is troponin (hs-TnI or hs-TnT) persistently elevated indicating ongoing myocyte injury (myocarditis etiology possible)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — troponin elevation in new-onset DCM suggests active myocarditis or inflammatory cardiomyopathy; triggers CMR for myocarditis LGE pattern (epicardial/mid-wall) and immunosuppression consideration

questions.question: Is there progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, exercise intolerance, or fluid retention (NYHA class II–IV)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — heart failure symptoms drive functional classification; NYHA III/IV is a high-risk marker and guides device therapy (ICD, CRT, LVAD) and transplant evaluation

questions.question: Is there a history of recent viral illness (within 4–6 weeks) preceding onset, or documented SARS-CoV-2 infection (post-COVID cardiomyopathy)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — viral myocarditis is the most common cause of new-onset DCM in children and young adults; post-COVID cardiomyopathy is an emerging etiology with partially reversible phenotype

high.label: 🔴  80–100 High confidence
high.action: DCM confirmed; initiate GDMT (ACEi/ARB/ARNI + beta-blocker + MRA + SGLT2i); genetic testing and family screening mandatory; assess for ICD (LVEF <35%) or CRT-D (LVEF <35% + LBBB); refer for transplant evaluation if refractory

moderate.label: 🟡  50–79 Moderate confidence
moderate.action: CMR indicated to confirm etiology, quantify EF, and assess fibrosis; troponin + inflammatory markers; genetic panel; rhythm monitoring (Holter); co-manage with pediatric heart failure specialist

low.label: 🟢  <50 Low confidence
low.action: echo with speckle-tracking strain analysis; exclude secondary causes (thyroid, tachycardia-induced, toxic, alcohol, nutritional); rule out physiologic LV dilation (athlete's heart), HCM phenocopy, or storage disease; repeat echo in 3 months
